**D. glycolysis is activated at the onset of exercise.** I'm changing my earlier answer. At exercise onset, glycolytic flux rises faster than oxidative metabolism can take up pyruvate, so pyruvate is converted to lactate more quickly. Falling pH is a consequence of lactate and H⁺ build-up, not a cause. The team note's two options don't fit the physiology: readily available oxygen lowers lactate production, and pyruvate is the substrate for lactate, so it has to be formed.

CONFIDENCE: 72
